title: Met Office autumn outlook: treat wet and wind as a temporary works load case, not a weather note
excerpt: The Met Office seasonal outlook issued around 11 September 2026 gives a higher-than-normal chance of a warm, wet UK autumn, with windy conditions more likely later in the season as a strong El Nino develops. That is not a forecast for any given Tuesday. It is a prompt for contractors to treat rainfall, reduced ground strength, flooded excavations, saturated platforms and out-of-service crane wind as temporary works load cases now, while there is still time to inspect, drain, re-brief and hold permits. Standard platforms and open-cut trenches do not automatically stay low risk when the ground is wet.
linkedinReady:
A seasonal outlook is not a lift plan and it is not a permit to load.

The Met Office 3-month outlook published this month gives a higher-than-normal chance of a warm, wet UK autumn, with windy conditions more likely later in the season as a strong El Nino develops. That does not tell you what happens on your site this week. It does tell the TWC and TWS to treat rainfall, saturated ground, flooded excavations and out-of-service crane wind as temporary works load cases before the first prolonged wet spell arrives.

HSE excavations guidance remains blunt: support or batter the sides, keep spoil and plant back from the edge, control groundwater and inspect after weather that can change the condition of the excavation. TWf2024:03 is equally clear that a granular working platform is only as good as the formation, drainage and maintenance that keep the design CBR available. CPA TIN 020 still sets a practical UK industry in-service limit of 38 mph (16.5 m/s) for tower cranes so there is time to weather-vane before the OEM out-of-service wind is reached.

Register platforms, excavations, hoardings, scaffolds and crane bases. Reinspect after rainfall. Do not assume last month's dry-weather permit still holds.

Educational only. Not for construction. Subject to the project temporary works procedure.

https://www.temporaryworksconsulting.com/news.html

body.p: On 11 September 2026 the Met Office restated its latest 3-month outlook: the chance of a warm and wet UK autumn is around one-and-a-half to two times higher than the climatological baseline, with an increased likelihood of windy conditions later in the season. Chief Meteorologist Ian Lisk linked the pattern to a developing El Nino already at near-record strength, while stressing that El Nino is only one driver and does not determine any particular day. BBC Weather and other outlets repeated the same primary Met Office position. This briefing does not treat the outlook as a site forecast. It treats it as a planning signal for temporary works items whose performance changes when the ground is wet and the wind rises.

Wet weather does not invent new temporary works. It changes the load path and the ground that the existing items rely on. Open excavations take water, lose face strength and attract surcharge from plant that can no longer use the planned haul route. Granular working platforms lose CBR when the formation is flooded or the surface is rutted. Hoardings, scaffold sheeting and temporary roofs pick up wind area that may not have been present when the item was first permitted. Tower cranes need time to be placed in the manufacturer's out-of-service condition; the industry in-service limit is not the same number as the design out-of-service wind. Standard does not automatically mean low risk. A shallow trench or a previously competent platform can become high consequence once groundwater, public interface or a crane is added. Provisional category only - to be confirmed by the TWC and the project temporary works procedure.

body.h: Practical TWC and TWS control points
ul: Add a weather-triggered review to the Temporary Works Register for excavations, working platforms, haul roads, hoardings, scaffold interfaces, temporary roofs, crane bases and outrigger pads.

Reinspect excavations after rainfall. Confirm support or batter, edge protection, stand-off of spoil and plant, dewatering and that nobody is working in an unsupported face. HSE excavations guidance is the statutory-duty starting point.

Walk every granular platform against TWf2024:03 principles: formation drainage, surface water run-off, rutting, contamination and whether the design plant still matches what is on site. A wet, rutted platform is a changed design.
Hold or re-issue permit to load / permit to use after exceptional weather. Last week's dry permit does not automatically survive standing water on the mat.
Confirm crane appointed-person limits against CPA TIN 020 (practical UK in-service 38 mph / 16.5 m/s for tower cranes) and the OEM out-of-service configuration, including free slew / weather-vaning.
Check hoarding, sheeted scaffold and temporary roof wind assumptions if the surrounding geometry has changed or if sheeting has been added since the original design.
Do not invent soil parameters or wind speeds. If GI, platform design CBR, plant data or crane charts are missing, stop and request them before recommending a change.
Independent check category remains provisional. Saturated ground, public interface, crane overturning and incomplete drainage normally point to escalation, not a CAT 1 close-out.

body.p: Educational briefing only. Not for construction. Not a design, not a check, not a weather forecast and not a permit. Subject to project-specific verification of drawings, loads, ground data, drainage, plant, crane charts, sequence and responsible persons, and to acceptance under the project temporary works procedure. Exact clause references in BS 5975-1:2024, BS EN 1997 and TWf2024:03 are to be confirmed against the project's licensed copy. AI-assisted drafting requires competent review before use on site. Do not proceed until reviewed and accepted by the competent person under the project temporary works procedure.
